title: SINGLE-SIDE LEGS · REDLINE
vibe: GREEN · THE SESSION YOU WERE WAITING FOR — the unilateral leg day you missed, loaded up and capped with a single-leg redline finisher. Two days off means fresh legs and a full send. No treadmill tempo today; your legs earn their burn from the iron.
why: You took 07-21 and 07-22 fully off — and that's exactly the true rest day the log had flagged as overdue after your 07-17 through 07-20 run block (four straight days with a 2-mile tempo each). So you don't come in beat up, you come in RECOVERED, which is precisely when we send it. You slept 6 (a touch short, so we keep the movements clean, not sloppy), nothing's sore, and you told me two things: get the unilateral work in, and get after it. Both, then. Session 1 is the single-side leg work you were looking forward to — kickstand RDL, front-rack reverse lunge, cossack, single-leg RDL — loaded to a real RPE 8 this time, not just a tempo groove. Your legs haven't had strength work since 07-18 (five days), so this fills a genuine gap on fresh legs. Then the get-after-it part: a for-time SINGLE-LEG REDLINE — Bulgarian split squats paired with heavy one-arm swings, pushed hard, minimal rest, heart rate through the roof. That IS your cardio today, which is why there's no 2-mile tempo: you've had zero pounding for two days, your legs are about to do serious strength AND a redline, and stacking a threshold run on top would just be junk impact. If you get the itch, an easy short jog to finish is your call — but the honest work is the iron. Cossack squat is your wildcard: you've literally never done it, and your adductors are about to find out.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day B (ankles / knees / hips) · prime single-leg + open the groin
blocks.text: Leg day on fresh legs — open the hips, ankles and knees and wake your balance. OS resets: diaphragmatic breathing x5 · rock-backs x10 · cross-crawls 10/side. Then Day B: deep-squat ankle rocks 10/side · toe-squat to heel-squat 8 · 90/90 hip switches 6/side · single-leg balance 20s/side · leg swings front-back + lateral 10/side · bodyweight cossack squat rehearsal 5/side to open the groin before you load it. Half of Session 1 is new to your joints — grease the pattern before you add weight, and your cossacks and single-leg RDLs will feel far more stable.

blocks.title: SESSION 1 · UNILATERAL LOWER (the work you wanted)
blocks.meta: ~20 min · 50 lb DB / 40 lb bell / 16 kg · single-side · RPE 8, controlled but pushed
blocks.format: TEMPO STRENGTH · 2 superset pairs, 3 rounds each · RPE 8 · 3-sec lowers, pause in the stretch · rest ~60s
blocks.workRest: Own each rep — 3 seconds down, real pause at the stretch, drive up — but load it and PUSH this time. Last set of each move: chase an extra rep or two past the target if form holds. All reps one side, then switch. Balance breaks or form breaks = that set's done.

items.name: A1 · Kickstand (B-Stance) RDL
items.detail: 50 lb DB · 10/side · working leg flat, back toe just kissing the floor for balance only (~20% of load). Hips BACK, feel the hamstring lengthen, pause, drive up. A single-leg RDL you can actually load heavy — go for it today.

items.name: A2 · Front-Rack Reverse Lunge
items.detail: 40 lb bell in the front rack (one side) · 8/side · step BACK, tall chest, knee to the floor, drive through the front heel. Front-rack loading lights the quad and forces the midline to stay stacked. Swap the rack side each set.

items.name: B1 · Cossack Squat (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg goblet · 8/side · wide stance, sink into ONE hip, other leg straight, foot flexed. Sit deep, chest up, drive back to center. Brutal on adductors + hip mobility — a movement you've NEVER done. Bodyweight the first round if depth fights you, then load it.

items.name: B2 · Single-Leg RDL
items.detail: 16 kg (same-side hand) · 8/side · slight bend in the standing knee, hinge and reach the bell down, back leg extends behind like a seesaw. Slow, feel the hamstring, no rounding. Balance IS the exercise.

blocks.text: The session you've been waiting for — every lift single-side, every lift new to your body, which is exactly the variety you asked for two days ago. Superset A (kickstand RDL + front-rack reverse lunge) is your loaded strength pair: hinge then squat, heavy, 3 rounds, ~60s rest. Superset B (cossack + single-leg RDL) attacks your frontal plane and your balance — the two qualities a year of swings and presses never touched. Difference from the tempo version I first wrote: you're rested now, so LOAD it and push to RPE 8, not just groove it. Cossack is the wildcard — sideways-plane strength nobody trains; expect soreness in new places. This is real leg work, and it sets up the redline to come.

blocks.title: SESSION 2 · LOADED ROTATION CORE (your daily core)
blocks.meta: ~7 min · 16 kg / 50 lb DB · dynamic midline — no planks, no hollows, no deadbugs
blocks.workRest: 3 unhurried rounds before the redline. Today the midline works through loaded BENDING and rotation, not stillness — different from your last core day. Control the weight, don't let it control you.

items.name: Kettlebell Windmill
items.detail: 16 kg overhead (locked out) · 5/side · eyes on the bell, push the same-side hip out, hinge and reach the free hand down your leg, stand tall. Loaded lateral flexion + thoracic rotation + hip mobility in one.

items.name: Half-Kneeling Halo
items.detail: 16 kg · 5 each direction/side · half-kneeling, circle the bell tightly around your head. The half-kneel makes your core fight to keep you from tipping while the load orbits. Switch the down-knee each round.

items.name: Suitcase Deadlift-to-Stand + Hold
items.detail: 50 lb DB one side · 6 reps then a 20s tall hold · deadlift from the floor on ONE side, stand fully, resist getting pulled sideways, then hold tall. Anti-lateral-flexion under real load. Switch sides each round.

blocks.text: Your dedicated daily core, done BEFORE the redline while you can still control the load. Steered away from your last core day's anti-rotation planks: today the windmill bends and rotates you under a locked-out bell, the half-kneeling halo makes your trunk resist tipping while the weight moves, and the suitcase deadlift-hold builds obliques that keep you upright against an offset load. All single-side — same theme as the leg block. Slow and deliberate; the core adapts to control, not speed.

blocks.title: GET-AFTER-IT FINISHER · SINGLE-LEG REDLINE
blocks.meta: ~9 min · 16 kg + 40 lb · FOR TIME · this is your cardio — push the pace
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS FOR TIME · RPE 9 · minimal rest · target under ~9 min
blocks.workRest: Move fast, rest only when your form demands it. This is the get-after-it you asked for — the swings spike your heart rate, the split squats bury your legs. Start the STOPWATCH and chase the clock.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.detail: 16 kg goblet (or bodyweight if legs are cooked) · 8/side · rear foot on a couch/bench, drop straight down, front knee tracks the toe, drive up. Rear-foot-elevated = your hardest single-leg quad burn, and after Session 1 your legs will already be screaming.

items.name: One-Arm Swing
items.detail: 40 lb · 12/side · explosive hip snap, bell to chest height, hand crushed on the handle. Heavy ballistic hinge — this is what drives your heart rate to the ceiling. Switch hands at 12.

blocks.text: The redline. A quad-dominant single-leg burn paired with a heavy explosive hinge, for time, three rounds, minimal rest — heart rate pinned, legs on fire. THIS is your cardio and your intensity today, which is exactly why there's no 2-mile tempo: you've had two days with zero pounding, and between heavy Session 1 and this redline your legs get everything they need without a single junk-impact mile. If you finish and genuinely need to run, keep it to an easy 8-10 min jog (~6 mph) — but you won't have much left, and that's the point. Get after it.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · open the hips, groin and hamstrings you just torched
blocks.text: Walk 60s to drop the heart rate. Then: deep half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch 30s/side · straddle / frog groin stretch 45s (the cossacks earned this) · standing or seated hamstring reach 30s/side · figure-4 glute stretch 30s/side · 5 slow nasal breaths. Report back: how the new single-side movements felt (especially the cossacks), your RPE on Session 1, your redline time, and whether the loaded-and-hard version delivered the get-after-it you wanted — that sets the intensity dial for next time.

timer.emomUnit: Session 1 = tempo reps by feel (3-sec lowers, ~60s rest). Finisher = STOPWATCH, 3 rounds for time, chase sub-9:00.
